title: Shanahan Talks Defensive Growth, Praises WR Mike Evans' Impact
headline: Mike Evans (Achilles soreness) missed practice and has no firm Monday status, Deebo Samuel (hamstring) may go to IR, and Nick Bosa (calf) is out.
summary: Shanahan opened with a long injury list. Deebo Samuel, Garret Wallow, Marques Sigle and Nick Bosa were all out, and Mike Evans was out with Achilles soreness and has an uncertain Monday status. Christian Kirk returned to practice for the first time after setbacks that began in training camp. Shanahan said IR is a real possibility for Samuel, and the bye week is the only reason the team is waiting. He said the coaches deliberately rotate Christian McCaffrey to keep him fresh, though early games dictated more of that than they expected. Jordan Watkins has earned the staff's respect with more opportunities because of the WR injuries, but Shanahan played down the stats. He praised Malik Mustapha's all-over-the-field play now that he is taking every rep. He called Washington, led by Jayden Daniels, probably the team's biggest challenge so far, and said the Evans-Brock Purdy connection has developed naturally and a bit faster than expected.

signals.note: He is out with a hamstring injury and is a bench or drop candidate if IR happens.

signals.note: Watch his status for IDP lineups.

signals.note: He is a deep-league flier while Samuel, Evans and Robinson are out, though Shanahan downplayed his production.

signals.note: Every-down snaps and a recent game MVP nod make him an IDP stream candidate.

signals.note: If Evans plays, the connection supports Purdy's passing production and Evans' target quality.

signals.note: He is not a short-term option and will not ease the WR shortage soon.
signals.quote: hoping to get him back after the bye week

topics.detail: Shanahan said Raheem Morris' scheme uses true zone drops and leaves DBs less able to count on linebackers underneath. That has made the secondary more aggressive and confident. He also credited the experience of Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green, Upton Stout and the safeties.
Shanahan said he sees Morris staying as long as he is in San Francisco. He worries about losing him to a head-coaching job but did not discuss an extension.

Shanahan said Daniels can be one of the league's better quarterbacks, with a natural pocket game and the speed to beat teams with his legs. He expects a hungry, desperate Washington team and called it probably the team's biggest challenge so far.
He said a short week before Atlanta is not a real factor. The calf recovery and re-injury risk for the returning players matter more.
Shanahan praised the punter's two strong weeks and joked about mistaking him for Malik. He also spoke warmly of learning leadership and 'brotherhood' from Dan Quinn.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/16/26
headline: Bill Croskey-Merritt's touches stay tied to game flow, while Austin Ekeler is back and Diggs and Percy Butler sat out Thursday's practice ahead of Monday night at SF.
summary: Quinn opened with injury returns: Trey Amos, Nick Cross and a third player (likely Jeremy McNichols) were worked back into practice last week and should have a full load. A linebacker (caption says 'Jordan McGee') starts his 21-day practice window. Quinn took full responsibility for the chaotic ending of Sunday's overtime game against the Giants. He said the team has turned the page, and he is making tweaks to game management and pre-snap discipline, including more officials at practice and fewer cadence variations. Asked about Croskey-Merritt's touches, he gave no promise and said they depend on the flow of runs, passes and the hot hand, though he praised the back's explosive power. He said Austin Ekeler's return adds a third-down and pass-game element who is most dangerous in space against safeties and linebackers, and that this will show more as the season goes on. Terry McLaurin was praised for playing through the game, while Stefon Diggs and Percy Butler (and another player whose name was unclear) did not practice but Quinn is hopeful they get reps later in the week. He described the 49ers (5-0) as a balanced, disciplined team where Kyle Shanahan is strongest on early downs with run actions, motions and shifts. He also said defenses are bringing more blitzes against his offense, and Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota can exploit man coverage with their backs turned.

signals.note: Quinn expressed full confidence in his mindset, which lowers any concern about his performance after the ending.
signals.quote: he is a really resilient guy

topics.detail: Quinn took full responsibility for the late-game management breakdowns in the overtime game vs. the Giants. The issues were dissected internally, and he plans tweaks to how game management is communicated.
More officials are at practice and the team is simplifying cadence usage to cut pre-snap penalties. The goal is to run plays at the line of scrimmage with normal cadences.

The defense played about 90 snaps in overtime. Quinn cited fourth-quarter breakdowns and said eye discipline in zone and man coverage and finishing in key moments are the fixes. He said Deatrich Wise (caption: 'Dietrich') made his presence felt in the run game in his return.
Opponents are blitzing more, especially later in games. Quinn said the offense needs built-in answers, and man coverage with backs turned can be an advantage for Daniels and Marcus Mariota.

San Francisco is 5-0 and balanced, limiting explosive plays on defense. Quinn called Shanahan exceptional on early downs and Brock Purdy off to a fast start, and he expects a physical game where avoiding self-inflicted mistakes matters most.
The players got an extra day off after a long trip and overtime. Quinn reminded the team that only about 30% of the season has been played.
